description: AsyncCounter loses updates under concurrent increment() calls due to a read-modify-write race; serialize increments.
prompt:
You are fixing a concurrency bug in JavaScript.

File: work/swe-04/counter.js

The exported class `AsyncCounter` has `increment()` (async, resolves to the value after increment) and `get()` (sync). Currently `increment()` does `const current = this.value; await delay(5); this.value = current + 1;` — concurrent calls all read the same `current`, so 20 concurrent increments end near `1` instead of `20`.

Requirements:
- Concurrent `increment()` calls must never lose updates: after `Promise.all` of N increments, the value must be exactly N.
- Each `increment()` must resolve to the counter value after its own increment (concurrent resolutions must be the unique values `1..N` in some order).
- Keep the public API (`new AsyncCounter()`, `async increment()`, `get()`) and use no external dependencies (a promise chain / mutex with built-ins is fine).

Edit work/swe-04/counter.js so the behavior above holds.
